overview: This single-page file consists of a State Department cross-reference sheet directing researchers to telegram no. 107 of April 6, 1932, filed at 894.50/61 (Section F). The referenced telegram from Edwin L. Neville in Japan reported that domestic copper prices were unsatisfactory, although the Japanese copper industry as a whole was said to remain in sound financial condition.

people.name: Edwin L. Neville
people.role: U.S. diplomat in Japan and sender of the referenced telegram

subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for telegram no. 107 on Japanese copper prices
subfiles.from: State Department file clerk; referencing a telegram from Edwin L. Neville
subfiles.about: The sheet redirects readers to a telegram reporting unsatisfactory copper prices but generally sound financial conditions in Japan's copper industry.
subfiles.summary: This filing note refers to telegram no. 107, sent from Japan by Neville at 4 p.m. on April 6, 1932, and directs the reader to decimal-file location 894.50/61, Section F. Its brief subject summary states that copper prices in Japan were unsatisfactory, while the industry as a whole was reportedly in good financial condition.

interest: The sheet is useful for reconstructing the State Department's dispersed filing of economic intelligence, since the substantive telegram was placed under another decimal-file number. Its précis also captures an important distinction between depressed commodity prices and the underlying financial health of Japan's copper industry during the global Depression.
